text:
liang: Heads-up — noticed a 12-18% p95 latency regression on the 8xA100 test harness after landing the KV-shard-to-TP change. Repro steps: local perf job with seq_len=1024, batch=1, TP=2, PP=2, DP=2.

liang: Quick profiling dump (rank0):
```
step 123: compute 128ms, attention_kv_fetch 42ms, NCCL allreduce 56ms, kernel(fused_attn) skipped -> fallback nonfused 31ms
KV traffic: 2.1GB per step (cross-TP allreduce bursts)
```

tara: Oof. That NCCL allreduce looks like the main offender. Did the change introduce an allreduce per-layer per-step? @omar any idea about PP interaction here?

omar: Yep. When KV is sharded by TP layer, we ended up with small-ish tensors being synced across TP ranks on every autoregressive step. With PP interleaved, some stages now wait for remote KV fragments before running, so compute/comm overlap drops.

omar: TLDR: TP-local KV -> more allreduces; DP replicate KV -> more memory but fewer syncs. PP complicates because pipeline flush points serialize the fetches.

maria: Suggest hybrid: shard KV within TP across devices for upper transformer blocks (those with big KV size) but replicate lower layers' KV across DP to avoid per-step reduction. We tried this pattern in staging and saw p95 improve ~8% on long sequences. Example config: 
```json
{"kv_shard_strategy":"hybrid","hybrid_rules":[{"layer_range":"0-11","placement":"dp_replicate"},{"layer_range":"12-23","placement":"tp_shard"}]}
```

david: Important note: kernel selector currently disables the fused attention kernel when KV buffers are non-contiguous across GPUs. That explains the "kernel(fused_attn) skipped" in your profile. We changed the kernel precondition in #3421 which didn't consider the new sharding layout.

liang: Ah. So regression is twofold: (1) extra NCCL overhead; (2) fallback to slower kernel. Makes sense.

tara: Two quick experiments to triage: 1) keep kernel selector pinned to fused_attn for TP-shard layouts and measure; 2) change NCCL schedule to group small allreduces (bucket) and test ncclAsync/allReduce reduce-scatter + allgather patterns. I'll try 1) today.

david: I can revert the kernel precondition for a canary build. If fused path is safe we should re-enable it conditionally when kv_shard_strategy != "per-layer-remote" and seq_len>512.

omar: Also try increasing the agg window in the batching heuristic so we batch more requests together — that reduces relative comm cost per token. But watch latency tail. For PLG demos we must keep p99 low.

liang: Good call. I ran a quick microbenchmark: turning on ncclGroup for small reduces cut allreduce overhead from ~56ms -> ~22ms on our 8x setup (non-ideal but promising).

sre-bot: perf-ci: nightly/8xA100/longseq reported regression +12% p95 after main merge. Linked: https://ci.redwood/perf/1749001234

prod-bot: deploy/canary started for fused-kernel-rollback build. CI green for basic unit tests. :thumbsup:

maria: Action items I propose:
- short (today): canary kernel precondition rollback (david) + nccl bucket experiment (tara) + microbench ncclGroup (liang)
- medium (48hrs): hybrid KV placement policy test matrix across TP/PP/DP dims (maria+omar)
- long: add kernel-selector heuristic and an automated perf guard that runs the 8x longseq harness on PRs touching KV placement/kernels.

liang: Agreed. I'll collect perf diffs and post a short summary in #eng-runtime once we have the canary numbers. Thanks all.

tara: tagging @david and @omar for visibility with support-hours request if needed.

david: Roger. I'll have a canary up in ~2hrs.

liang: Thanks.

prod-bot: perf-canary result: fused-rollback-canary -> p95 -9%, p99 -3% (prelim). More thorough runs in progress.

liang: Nice. We'll re-run with hybrid configs next and keep an eye on memory vs latency trade-offs.
